subject: Clarify SIG question on privileged access and keystore ownership - Finlex
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finlex.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finlex.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG Q: privileged access / keystore scope (Q42) - need clarification

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking SIG submissions — we started filling out the Finlex SIG and hit an ambiguous wording in Q42 (attached). The text reads: "Are privileged access controls applied to components that can modify key material or key policies?" It's not clear whether this is intended to capture short-lived orchestrator node creds (ephemeral container admin) that have the ability to call the management API to rotate keys, or only long-lived operator/service accounts that are explicitly labeled as "Key Admin".

Couple of asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether ephemeral/orchestrator credentials are considered "privileged access" for Q42?
- If yes, what's the recommended evidence (audit trail / sample logs) we should request?

Attached: our copy of the SIG template (SIG_Finlex_v3.xlsx) with the Q42 cell highlighted and a small network diagram.

We can schedule a short call if useful — we have a security sync window tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Security
Finlex Capital

Attachment: SIG_Finlex_v3.xlsx (xlsx), network-diagram.png (png)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finlex.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q: privileged access / keystore scope (Q42) - need clarification

Alex,

Thanks for the clear note and the file. Short answer: this is a great question and the wording can be ambiguous depending on how "modify key material" is interpreted. Longer answer below and happy to jump on a 20-minute call. I copied Michael (infra) and Soojin (security lead) so they can provide the precise interpretation we use for SIG evidence.

High-level we treat any principal (ephemeral or long-lived) that can perform management-plane operations on customer encryption keys or key policies as "privileged" for SIG purposes. That includes orchestrator node credentials if they can call APIs that rotate or change key state.

Suggested next steps:
- Quick call to confirm your environment examples (20 min).
- We'll follow up with a written interpretation and the exact evidence mapping (audit/CloudTrail samples, API call names, retention window).

Proposed times: Fri 8:30–10:00 PST or Mon 9:00–11:00 PST. Which works for you?

Evelyn
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

(Signature)
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finlex.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finlex.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q: privileged access / keystore scope (Q42) - need clarification

Evelyn — thanks.

We can do Fri 9:00 PST. For context: our orchestrator spins up short-lived nodes that have a bootstrap token allowing them to call the Redwood management API (rotateKey(), setKeyPolicy()). The tokens expire in 30 minutes. We also have long-lived service accounts that can do the same for automation jobs.

On the evidence side, we'd expect to collect API logs showing who called rotateKey() and the requestor principal. If Redwood considers ephemeral tokens "privileged" we'll map those calls as well.

I'll send a calendar invite for Fri 9:00 PST.

Regards,
Alex
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finlex.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q: privileged access / keystore scope (Q42) - interpretation and evidence mapping

Alex — good to meet this morning. Per our call, here is the written interpretation and concrete evidence we typically provide for SIG Q42. Please consider this our formal response you can include in your SIG spreadsheet.

1) Interpretation (plain language):
- For SIG Q42, "privileged access" should be interpreted to include any principal (ephemeral or long-lived) capable of performing management-plane operations that create, rotate, import, or modify key material or key policy.
- Short-lived/orchestrator credentials are included when they possess the API privileges described above.

2) Recommended explicit SIG answer (what to put in the SIG cell):
- "Yes — privileged access controls are applied to any principal able to modify key material or key policies, including short-lived orchestrator nodes when those nodes possess key-management API privileges."

3) Evidence we can provide and how it's mapped to the SIG:
- Audit trail sample (CloudTrail / Redwood management logs) showing API calls: rotateKey, importKey, putKeyPolicy, scheduleKeyDeletion. (Attachment: evidence-sample.pdf)
- User/principal mapping document showing role-to-permission mapping and TTL for ephemeral tokens (we provide a redacted CSV extract).
- Config excerpt from our IAM/orchestration plane showing how tokens are provisioned and TTLs.
- Network diagram (network-diagram.png) included to show control-plane segmentation.

4) Retention/coverage notes:
- Audit logs are retained for 13 months in customer-facing reports.
- We redact customer PII from artifacts before sending.

5) Action items we agreed on:
- Redwood: export a 7-day sample of management-plane API logs that correspond to rotateKey and putKeyPolicy calls (redacted). -> Michael to own.
- Finlex: confirm which environment (prod vs staging) you want evidence from and provide an inbox for artifacts. -> Alex to confirm.

Attachments: evidence-sample.pdf (pdf) — contains redacted CloudTrail snippets and example principal IDs.

If you want, we'll also provide a one-page summary you can drop into your SIG comments column.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
